svg.text: claudia composes — ordered and unordered lists
Proposal for review — nothing is built. A list item is a paragraph with a (list, level) mark; the bullet or number is drawn from the list's scheme and derived, never typed.
A · the text in Flow view
The caret is in item 2 of a numbered list, so the “numbered” toggle is pressed. Level 1 of numbers is a., b.; level 1 of bullets is ◦.
Before people arrive, three things need to be in place:
Chairs in a circle, not rows
Eight is enough for the first round
On the day itself, in this order:
Welcome and a short round of names
Remark: check the room booking before sending this.
Collect the results and share them
Two toggles and indent / outdent in the toolbar. The same
entries are in Format ▸ List (B), so native menus have them.
Bullets and numbers are drawn beside the text. They are not
characters: search, copy, the AI and the authorship view
Numbers are derived from the list, never typed. Add, move
or delete an item and the others renumber.
Nested numbers restart under each parent (a., b.). Tab and
A note between two items does not end the list: item 4 is
still the same list and keeps counting.
Items keep their paragraph style (Body text, Quote…): a list
adds structure, not a look. Indent and spacing come from the
list's scheme, one definition for every list that uses it.
One new entry in composes' Format menu, between “All styles…” and “Colours…”.
It acts on the selected paragraphs, or the one with the caret.
Ticked: every selected paragraph is such an item; choosing it again takes the list away.
“Continue previous list” is active only on the first item of a list when an earlier list
with the same kind of numbers exists; “Start at…” asks for the first number.
Every key press is one ordinary command in the history: undoable, and locked
like any other edit of that paragraph.
In an item: a new item below, same list and level.
On an empty item: outdent one level; at level 0 leave the list.
Indent one level, if the item above is as deep or deeper.
Shift+Tab outdents; at level 0 it does nothing.
At the start of an item: outdent, then leave the list.
Only after that does it join with the paragraph above.
Bullets / numbers for the selection: a new list. On a whole list
of the other kind it changes that list instead.
Typing “- ” or “1. ” to start a list; dragging items; editing a
scheme (formats, indent, gap) — that is the enumeration manager.
· A list is the items that share one list. Items of two lists never count together,
even when they are neighbours; a note between items of one list does not split it.
· Counting is per level: a level starts again after an item of a shallower level;
a missing parent counts as none.
· Numbers go 1. a. i. and then round again, bullets • ◦ ▪ and round again; nine levels.
D · The same mechanism, later (concept — no screen is designed here)
What lists add is a label that is derived from structure. Numbered headings, “see section 2.1” and a table of contents need exactly that, so the model keeps the seam open.
in the kernel, run after structural
beside the text · in a reference that stores the paragraph id
and shows its current label · in the table of contents ·
in the exports (ODT, docx, LaTeX, Markdown)
A reference never holds a typed number. Move a step and the reference follows; delete it and the reference is shown as broken, not silently stale.
